flock_freight_2024_whitepaper.key_findings: 2023 data: average LTL damage rate 1.94% (1 in 51 shipments); largest enterprise shippers incurred up to $6.3M annually in damage and loss claims. Average cost per claim $3,777. Footnote 1: 'Source: 2023 Drive Research Study & Flock claims data'. Methodology: 1,000-respondent online survey conducted by Drive Research (third party), Feb–Apr 2024, 57 questions, 95% confidence level ±3% margin of error.
flock_freight_2024_whitepaper.notes: The $6.3M figure is the upper bound for the largest shippers (company size $3B+). The 1.94% is the 2023 damage rate from this study. This study does NOT contain the 1.24% figure.

flock_freight_2025_study.key_findings: 2024 data: average LTL damage rate 1.24% (1 in 80 shipments); largest shippers incurred up to $5.1M in damage and loss claims in 2024. Average cost per claim $1,796. Same Drive Research methodology.
flock_freight_2025_study.notes: PDF empty on markitdown. Figures corroborated by search snippet. This is the source of the 1.24% and $5.1M figures. $5.1M is the upper bound for large shippers in 2024.

synchrogistics_claims_index.notes: The Synchro LTL Claims Ratio Index uses a different metric: claims paid ($) / carrier revenue = 0.34–0.35% in Q1–Q2 2025. This is NOT the same as the shipment damage incidence rate (1.24%). The two metrics measure fundamentally different things and should not be conflated.

ata_trucking_org.notes: ATA publishes American Trucking Trends (annual). ATA also has freight claims law review events. No freely accessible published LTL damage rate statistics found. Paywall/membership required for detailed data.

bts_freight_facts.notes: BTS Freight Facts and Figures covers freight movement volumes and transportation system performance, not carrier claims rates.

nmfta.notes: NMFTA is focused on freight classification (NMFC codes), not aggregate damage rate statistics. No published damage-rate data found.

tia_tianet.notes: TIA publishes 3PL market reports and covers cargo claims topics, but survey data is members-only and not publicly indexed.

marsh_aig_travelers.notes: No publicly available Marsh, AIG, or Travelers LTL cargo damage rate report found. Insurance industry cargo loss data not publicly published in accessible form.

critical_finding: The claim conflates two separate Flock Freight surveys: the 1.24% damage rate and $5.1M figure come from the 2025 study (reporting 2024 data), while the $6.3M figure comes from the 2024 study (reporting 2023 data). When combined as '$5.1-$6.3M', the range spans two different survey years (2023 and 2024). The 2024 study reported 1.94%, not 1.24%. So '1.24%' and '$5.1-$6.3M' cannot be used as a single coherent data point — they originate from different year surveys. Both surveys are vendor-authored (Flock Freight, an LTL alternative carrier that profits from demonstrating LTL is problematic), conducted via Drive Research (legitimate third-party firm), with 1,000-respondent samples. No government, multilateral, academic, or major insurer source confirms these specific figures. The Synchrogistics claims ratio (0.34–0.35%) uses a revenue-denominated metric that is not comparable.

suggested_revision_options.revised_claim_text: [ASSUMED-N based on Flock Freight/Drive Research shipper surveys]: LTL freight damage incidence rate was reported at 1.24% of shipments in 2024 (down from 1.94% in 2023), with the largest enterprise shippers ($3B+ revenue) incurring up to $5.1M annually in damage and loss claims — to validate: ATA American Trucking Trends data purchase, TIA member survey, or Marsh/Aon cargo loss actuarial data
suggested_revision_options.rationale: The 1.24% and $5.1M figures come exclusively from a single vendor-sponsored shipper survey (Flock Freight 2025 study). No independent primary source confirms these figures. The combined '$5.1-$6.3M' range is also misleading as it spans two different survey years.

suggested_revision_options.revised_claim_text: LTL freight damage incidence rates are reported in the range of 1-2% of shipments by industry surveys, with enterprise shippers potentially incurring millions annually in claims costs — specific figures vary materially by methodology and company size.
suggested_revision_options.rationale: The 1-2% range for LTL damage rates appears consistently across multiple logistics industry sources (including Nuvocargo benchmarks and multiple blog-cited industry benchmarks), even if no single government or academic source publishes it. The wider range is defensible.

The specific 1.24% and $5.1-$6.3M figures are too precisely vendor-sourced and methodologically fragile (vendor survey, cross-year conflation) to be stated as fact in a primary research artifact without clearer caveating.

reasoning: No government agency (BTS, ATA-published public data), insurer (Marsh, Travelers, AIG), multilateral, or academic source publishes a verifiable LTL shipment damage rate. The specific 1.24% and $5.1-6.3M figures trace exclusively to Flock Freight vendor-commissioned surveys (Drive Research, 1,000 respondents), where Flock Freight has a commercial interest in demonstrating LTL damage is costly. The cross-year conflation of the range ($5.1M from 2025 study / 2024 data; $6.3M from 2024 study / 2023 data) further weakens the claim's precision. The claim should be marked ASSUMED-N with a validation path to ATA Trucking Trends, TIA membership data, or insurer actuarial sources.
